title: Versioned flighting and health safeguards for VPC private deployments
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Goal: Deliver an automated, auditable 'flighting' system for private (VPC) control plane version promotions that integrates with our Terraform modules, enforces runtime compatibility checks, runs progressive health probes, and automates safe rollback. This ticket covers orchestration glue, new IaC entrypoints, canary cohort selection, telemetry-driven promotion gating, and an operator playbook for on-call intervention.

Why: Customers running Redwood Private need predictable, low-risk upgrades that do not require manual steps across tenants and private networks. Current upgrade steps are manual and error-prone for the control plane in customer VPCs. A flighting model reduces blast radius while enabling predictable promotions for security and feature releases.

Scope:
- New Terraform module inputs for declaring a versioned control plane artifact and traffic split policy.
- Orchestrator (extension to the control plane operator) to manage staged promotions and shard-level promotions inside customer VPCs.
- Health probe harness: liveness, readiness, telemetry delta (latency, error-rate), and drift detection for config sync.
- Automatic rollback and safe-hold triggers based on configurable SLO deltas.
- Audit logs and a step-by-step operator console flow in the Redwood Console for private customers.
- Integration tests (local e2e harness + CI against a small set of private cluster fixtures).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes 'control_plane_version', 'flight_cohorts', and 'probe_policy' inputs and documents defaults.
Orchestrator can promote a new version to a named cohort (eg. cohort-A 5% traffic) and automatically expand cohorts when health gates pass.
Health gates evaluated by telemetry: 95th latency, 5xx rate, and KV cache miss ratio; promotion halts if any gate exceeds configured thresholds.
Automatic rollback procedure triggers within 5 minutes of a gate breach and records rollback reason in audit logs.
End-to-end tests validate promotion, expansion, and rollback flows using a reproducible terraform plan on a test VPC fixture.
Runbook and console UI tooltips updated; SREs and Solutions Engs have a playbook for manual override and emergency promotion cancel.
Security review completed and KMS keys usage documented for artifact signing and provenance checks.

comments: 2026-03-10 — Asha Mehta: Kickoff meeting notes attached. We agreed to scope MVP to 3 cohort stages (5%, 25%, 100%) with a manual opt-in flag per tenant. Action: Design to propose a compact state model that minimizes cross-tenant operator coordination.

2026-03-11 — Liam O'Connor: Implemented initial terraform module prototype in git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra-modules.git#feature/flighting. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/412. Module exposes 'flight_cohorts' as a map and 'probe_policy' as a string reference to a named policy in the console.

2026-03-11 — Priya Patel (SRE): Telemetry gating proposal posted. Using delta-based checks vs baseline to reduce false positives during noise. Proposed gates: p95 latency delta > 30%, 5xx rate increase > 0.5pp, kv_cache_miss increase > 10%.

2026-03-12 — Security review (Alex Wu): flagged artifact signing as required for private customer trust. We will add a KMS signing step in the release pipeline and operator will verify signature before promotion.

2026-03-12 — Liam O'Connor: Began operator scaffold. Current TODO: idempotent promotion step and durable checkpointing to reconcile operator restarts. Planning to use tenant-scoped CustomResourceDefinition 'VersionFlight' to model progress.
notes: Trade-offs: we evaluated both traffic proxying (layer-7 split) and host-based cohort pinning. Proxying provides transparent split but requires extra network hops inside VPCs; host pinning is simpler but needs durable mapping. For MVP we chose proxy-based 5% cohorts for minimal application changes. Next iteration will evaluate host pinning for lower latency.
next_steps: Complete terraform module PR reviews, merge operator scaffold behind a feature flag, add signed artifact checks in the release pipeline, and schedule a dry-run on a consenting pilot customer VPC in mid-March.
implementation_risks: Private network egress/configuration differences between customers may cause flaky e2e tests
Telemetry noise leading to false rollbacks if baselines are not calibrated per tenant
Operator permissions in customer VPCs could be constrained by customer IAM policies — need clear install-time checklist
